correctness.rationale: For every normalized convex f, classical curvature subordination gives omega=uz+vz^2+... with |v|<=1-\(|u|^2\). Explicit Taylor expansion and local reversion give \(\gamma_2=u^2/4+v/6\) and \(\Gamma_2=u^2/4-v/6\). Applying reverse triangle inequalities bounds the signed modulus mismatch in absolute value by 2min(\(|u|^2\)/4,(1-\(|u|^2\))/6). Every signed endpoint is realized by omega=z(u+lambda z)/(1+conj(u)lambda z), with lambda of modulus at most one. Continuity yields the full attainable interval. The envelope is maximized uniquely at \(|u|^2\)=2/5; equality and Schwarz–Pick classify the unique two rotated Blaschke families. Both gamma/Gamma cancellation cases are checked. A standalone exact symbolic checker reproduced the identities and numerical cases; finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The forward-inverse comparison of logarithmic coefficients is a motivated sharp-invariance question arising from contemporary papers, but separately sharp successive-index bounds leave the paired same-function mismatch unanswered. The full exact interval at each complex second Taylor coefficient, the unique transition from r/2 to (1-r)/3 at r=2/5, and the complete equality/cancellation family together form a natural classification across the entire convex class, not an arbitrary finite slice.
